senses.gloss:
Yayāti is mentioned twice in the Rigveda, once as an ancient sacrificer, and once as Nahuṣya, ‘descendant of Nahuṣa,’ apparently a king. There is no trace whatever of his connexion with pūru, as in the Epic, the tradition of which must be deemed to be inaccurate.
Foot notes i. 31, 17; x. 63, 1.
Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 147; Muir, Sanskrit Texts 12, 232.

Yāyāvara denotes a person of no fixed abode in the yajurveda Saṃhitās.
Foot notes Literally, ‘wandering about,’ from the intensive of yā, ‘to go.’
taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 2, 1, 7; kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xix. 12.
